skill.name: parametric-scribe
skill.description: Records coding steps in a recipe file so agents can replay, adapt, or fork previous work.
skill.summary: Track coding history as replayable recipe steps for AI-assisted development.
skill.author: Cycleaddict

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown backtick false positives, not Ruby or shell execution. One real external command risk remains because the replay workflow instructs git checkout, and two semantic risks involve prompt retention and replaying recipe-sourced prompts.

remediation.issue: Replay workflow changes repository state with git checkout.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation, verify a clean working tree, and create a branch or backup before running checkout.

remediation.issue: Recipe entries store exact user prompts.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to redact credentials, customer data, and private context before saving or sharing recipe files.

remediation.issue: Replay uses prompts read from recipe history.
remediation.suggestion: Treat recipe files from repositories or collaborators as untrusted and review steps before executing replay.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Prompt Retention
semantic_findings.description: The recipe format stores the exact prompt used for each step. If prompts contain secrets or private data, docs/recipe.yaml can retain sensitive information.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented YAML entry includes a prompt field that records the exact prompt. The risk depends on user content, so confidence is high for retention behavior but lower for actual exposure.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Recipe Prompt Replay
semantic_findings.description: The replay protocol reads original prompts from the recipe and executes adapted prompts. A tampered recipe file could steer the agent during replay.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The protocol directly reads recipe content and later executes adapted prompts from that history. The threat requires an untrusted or modified recipe file, so the confidence is moderate.

content.value_statement: Coding agents usually lose the reasoning behind each step. Parametric Scribe records prompts, outputs, and SHAs so teams can replay or fork work.
actual_capabilities: Records completed coding tasks as entries in docs/recipe.yaml.
Stores each step intent, prompt, output files, timestamp, and git SHA.
Defines a replay workflow for changing an earlier step.
Guides agents to adapt later steps when project files change.
Defines a fork workflow using a copied recipe file.
limitations: Requires the agent to maintain recipe.yaml consistently.
Replay depends on valid git SHAs and a clean working tree.
Does not include an executable tool or validation script.
Stored prompts may contain sensitive details unless users redact them.

use_cases.title: Prototype Direction Changes
use_cases.description: Replay an early framework or architecture decision and adapt later work instead of rebuilding from scratch.

use_cases.title: Review Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Inspect prompts, outputs, and SHAs for each coding step during team review.

use_cases.title: Create Feature Variants
use_cases.description: Fork a recipe to test a different implementation path while preserving the original history.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Recipe
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin a new project with recorded coding history.
prompt_templates.prompt: Read parametric-scribe/SKILL.md. After each coding task, update docs/recipe.yaml with the step intent, files changed, and current git SHA.

prompt_templates.title: Record a Completed Task
prompt_templates.scenario: Capture a finished change as the next recipe step.
prompt_templates.prompt: Record the completed task as the next recipe step. Include the intent, the user prompt, changed files, timestamp, and current commit reference.

prompt_templates.title: Replay an Earlier Step
prompt_templates.scenario: Change a previous implementation decision and adapt later work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Replay from Step [number] with this new prompt: [new direction]. Before checkout, confirm the branch, clean working tree, and target SHA.

prompt_templates.title: Fork a Variant Safely
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare two implementation paths while preserving the original recipe.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a variant recipe for Step [number]. Keep the original recipe unchanged, apply this alternate prompt, and summarize changed downstream steps.

output_examples.input: User asks to record a completed authentication task.
output_examples.output: The agent adds a recipe entry describing the intent, changed files, timestamp, and current commit reference.

output_examples.input: User asks to change Step 002 from Flask to FastAPI.
output_examples.output: The agent reviews the recipe, asks for confirmation before changing git state, reruns the target step, and adapts later steps.

output_examples.input: User asks to create a variant for a different storage backend.
output_examples.output: The agent copies the recipe into a variant file and changes only the selected path for comparison.

best_practices: Review the recipe after important tasks to keep intent and outputs accurate.
Confirm a clean working tree before any replay or checkout action.
Redact secrets from prompts before storing or sharing the recipe.
anti_patterns: Running replay commands without user confirmation.
Treating recipe prompts from unknown repositories as trusted instructions.
Storing API keys, credentials, or private customer data in recorded prompts.

faq.question: Does this skill run code by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow instructions for an AI coding agent to follow.

faq.question: What file does it maintain?
faq.answer: It maintains docs/recipe.yaml as the source of truth for step history.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it replace Git?
faq.answer: No. It depends on Git SHAs to identify earlier project states.

faq.question: What should I check before replay?
faq.answer: Check the current branch, confirm a clean working tree, and verify the target SHA.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive prompts?
faq.answer: Use caution. The recipe can store exact prompts, so redact secrets before saving or sharing it.
